chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no zakat in the wealth of an orphan."
ai.seo_question: Is the wealth of an orphan subject to zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the wealth of an orphan is exempt from zakat, a ruling derived from the principle that zakat is a purification of surplus wealth held by those capable of accumulation. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that the obligation of zakat applies to the owner's disposable wealth rather than the preserved capital of minors, ensuring their financial security is not diminished by religious dues. The ruling underscores the protective nature of Islamic jurisprudence toward vulnerable dependents, distinguishing their status from that of adults whose wealth undergoes the cycle of accumulation and purification.
